display.title: The Alter Rebbe and the Stolen Logs, Part 2 (Rosh Hashanah)
display.summary_short: Why Rosh Hashanah falls on the day Adam was created, why we must never waste time, and how listening to the Alter Rebbe saved an honest Chassid's life.
display.summary_long: After a recap of the honest Chassid framed for stealing logs, the storyteller asks his class why Rosh Hashanah marks the creation of Adam and not the first day of creation: the world was made so that people could serve Hashem, just as a Jew's true age counts only the years he serves Hashem. Hashem created Adam last, like a guest invited only when the meal is ready, which teaches us never to waste time; a funny story about a boy who lost a dime shows that a lost hour cannot be made up. Every Jew must feel that the world was created for him. Back in the story, the Alter Rebbe tells Reb Baruch to go to the minister now. The minister greets him warmly: an officer had been waiting the week before to shoot him on sight, and since then witnesses revealed that Alex planted the logs. The storyteller connects this to trusting the Rebbe in our own times, including during the COVID pandemic, and to the Rebbe's promise that Moshiach is about to come.
display.lesson: Use every moment Hashem gives you, and when you follow a tzaddik's instructions with bitachon, only good comes of it.

date.note: The week after Chai Elul; hopes for the Geulah 'before Rosh Hashanah comes'; COVID talk fits 5780.
